book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 24 · Head and Face Injuries
title: Face, Eye and Neck Injuries: Airway First
next: Chapter 24, Lesson 2: Head injuries, traumatic brain injury and the BC TBI protocol

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already open the airway with a jaw thrust, suction, control bleeding and protect the spine. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Treat face and neck injuries as airway problems first
  2. Assess and protect injured eyes, ears, teeth and necks
  3. Know what the PCP adds, and the BC rules for these wounds

Textbook: Chapter 24, PDF pages 1972–2057
slides.say: Welcome back. As EMRs, you already protect the spine, open the airway with a jaw thrust, suction, and control bleeding. Now that you're practising as a PCP, you'll look deeper. Today is the first half of Chapter twenty-four: injuries of the face, eyes, ears, mouth, and the front of the neck. We have three goals. First, treat every face and neck injury as an airway problem first. Second, assess and protect injured eyes, ears, teeth, and necks the right way. Third, know exactly what the PCP adds, and which BC rules apply.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。作为 EMR，你们已经会保护脊柱、用推颌法开放气道、吸引和止血。现在以 PCP 身份执业，你要看得更深。今天讲第二十四章的前半部分：面部、眼、耳、口腔和颈前部的损伤。三个目标：第一，把每个面部和颈部损伤首先当成气道问题；第二，用正确的方法评估和保护受伤的眼、耳、牙齿和颈部；第三，清楚 PCP 具体多做什么，以及适用哪些 BC 规定。

slides.title: A face injury is a warning sign
slides.body:
The face rarely kills, but it warns you

  • Maxilla fracture needs up to 150 g → think brain + C-spine
  • Significant head injury = C-spine injury until proven otherwise
  • Fracture signs: malocclusion, asymmetry, crepitus, loose bones
  • Check eye movement: can't look up → orbit or cheekbone fracture
  • No need to name the fracture type — that takes a CT
slides.say: Facial cuts look dramatic, but alone they rarely kill. What they do is warn you. Breaking the maxilla, the upper jaw, can take up to one hundred fifty g, that is, one hundred fifty times the pull of gravity. A force that strong often injures the brain and the cervical spine too, so treat a significant head or face injury as a spinal injury until proven otherwise. Look for malocclusion, which means the teeth don't line up, an uneven face, crepitus, or loose bones. If one eye can't look up, think of an orbit or cheekbone fracture.
slides.sayZh: 面部伤口看着吓人，但单独很少致命，它的作用是提醒你。打断上颌骨可能需要高达一百五十 g 的力，也就是一百五十倍重力。这么大的力常常同时伤到脑和颈椎，所以明显的头面部损伤在排除之前都按脊柱损伤处理。要找咬合不正，也就是上下牙对不齐，还有面部不对称、骨擦感或骨头松动。如果一只眼不能往上看，要想到眼眶或颧骨骨折。

slides.title: Airway first: blood, bones and teeth
slides.body:
1. Hold the head in line; jaw thrust
  2. Remove broken teeth and dentures; suction
  3. Adequate breathing → O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  4. Inadequate → BVM with 100% O₂
  5. Heavy bleeding: suction ≤ 15 s, ventilate ~2 min, repeat

Object through the cheek blocking the airway: remove it the way it went in, gauze inside the cheek, pressure outside.
slides.say: Your first job is the airway. Hold the head in line and use a jaw thrust. Remove broken teeth or dentures and suction the blood. If breathing is adequate, give oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four percent or higher; if not, ventilate with a bag-valve mask and one hundred percent oxygen. With heavy bleeding, alternate: suction up to fifteen seconds, then ventilate about two minutes. Loose facial bones make the mask seal hard, so get a second rescuer. And an object through the cheek that blocks the airway comes out the way it went in; then pack the cheek and press from outside.
slides.sayZh: 第一件事是气道。手法保持头部中立，用推颌法。取出断牙或假牙，吸引血液。呼吸足够时给氧，使血氧维持在九十四以上；不够时用球囊面罩加百分之百氧通气。出血多时交替进行：吸引最多十五秒，再通气约两分钟。面骨松动会让面罩难以密封，所以要第二个人帮忙。还有，穿透面颊并堵塞气道的异物，顺着进入的方向取出，然后颊内塞纱布、外面加压。

slides.title: The nose: blood or clear fluid?
slides.body:
Nosebleed (epistaxis)Clear fluid (CSF) after head trauma
Pinch the nostrils firmlyDon't try to stop the flow
Awake, no spine concern: sit up, lean forwardLoose sterile dressing only
Unresponsive: on the side, if the spine allowsNo nasal airway, nothing in the nose

Older adults on blood thinners can bleed from the back of the nose: swallowed, hidden, and enough to cause shock.
slides.say: The nose gives you two different problems. For a nosebleed, or epistaxis, pinch the nostrils firmly. If the patient is awake and the spine isn't a concern, sit them up and lean them forward, so blood drains out, not down the throat. Clear fluid from the nose or ears after head trauma is different. It may be cerebrospinal fluid, the fluid around the brain, which means a skull fracture. Don't block it; that may raise the pressure in the skull. Cover it loosely, and never insert a nasal airway, which could pass through the fracture into the brain.
slides.sayZh: 鼻子会给你两种不同的问题。鼻出血时，用力捏住鼻翼。病人清醒、不担心脊柱时，让他坐起身体前倾，血往外流而不是流进喉咙。头部受伤后鼻子或耳朵流出清亮液体就不一样了：那可能是脑脊液，也就是包着脑的液体，说明有颅骨骨折。不要堵住它，否则可能升高颅内压。只用松的敷料盖住，绝不能放鼻咽通气道，它可能穿过骨折进入脑内。

slides.q: After an assault, a man has an unstable midface and clear, blood-tinged fluid running from his nose. He is drowsy and snoring. Which action should you AVOID?
options: Jaw thrust with manual stabilization of the head
Placing a loose dressing under the nose
slides.say: Time for a question. After an assault, a man has an unstable midface and clear, blood-tinged fluid running from his nose. He is drowsy and snoring. Which action should you avoid? A, a jaw thrust with manual stabilization of the head. B, suctioning blood from the mouth. C, inserting a nasopharyngeal airway. D, placing a loose dressing under the nose. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停下来做道题。一名男子被殴打后，面中部骨头松动，鼻子流出带血的清亮液体，他昏昏欲睡、有鼾声。下列哪项应该避免？A 推颌法并手法固定头部；B 吸引口腔里的血；C 放置鼻咽通气道；D 在鼻子下面放一块松的敷料。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. Clear fluid from the nose after head trauma suggests a skull fracture, and a nasal airway could pass through the fracture into the skull; use an oral airway instead if he tolerates it. A is correct airway care when a spinal injury is possible. B keeps the airway clear of blood. D is right too: you cover the fluid loosely, but you don't try to stop it.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。头部外伤后鼻子流清亮液体提示颅骨骨折，鼻咽通气道可能穿过骨折进入颅内；如果他能耐受，改用口咽通气道。A 是可能有脊柱损伤时正确的气道处理；B 保持气道没有血；D 也对：液体只用松敷料盖住，不要试图堵住。

slides.title: Eye injuries: the PCP exam
slides.body:
• Vision loss that doesn't clear with blinking: most serious symptom
  • Double vision → eye muscles caught, often an orbit fracture
  • Check orbit, lids, cornea, conjunctiva, globe, pupils, movement
  • Visual acuity: each eye separately, and document it
  • About 20% of people have slightly unequal pupils normally
  • No reaction, no movement? Ask about an artificial eye
slides.say: As a PCP, your eye exam needs to be organized. Start with symptoms. Vision loss that doesn't improve with blinking is the most important; it may mean damage to the eyeball or the optic nerve. Double vision suggests trapped eye muscles, often from an orbit fracture. Then check the orbit, lids, cornea, conjunctiva, globe, pupils, and movement in every direction. Test visual acuity roughly, one eye at a time, and document it. Two traps: about one person in five has slightly unequal pupils normally, and an eye that doesn't react or move may be artificial, so ask.
slides.sayZh: 作为 PCP，你的眼部检查要有条理。先问症状。眨眼也不能改善的视力丧失最重要，可能是眼球或视神经受损。复视提示眼外肌被卡住，常因眼眶骨折。然后检查眼眶、眼睑、角膜、结膜、眼球、瞳孔，以及各个方向的眼球运动。粗测视力，两眼分别测，并记录下来。两个陷阱：大约五个人里就有一个人两侧瞳孔天生略不等大；一只对光没反应、也不跟着动的眼睛可能是义眼，问一下就好。

slides.title: Protecting an injured eye
slides.body:
• Never press on an injured globe
  • Rigid shield; cover both eyes (they move together)
  • Impaled object: leave it; cup over it, secure it
  • Eye out of the socket: moist sterile dressing; never push it back
  • Hyphema or ruptured globe: head up 30–40° (book)
  • Collar not too tight; prevent coughing and vomiting

Both eyes covered = a scared patient who can't see. Keep talking.
slides.say: The rule for an injured eyeball: never press on it. Pressure can squeeze out the vitreous humour, the jelly at the back of the eye, and it doesn't come back. Use a rigid shield and cover both eyes, because the eyes move together. An impaled object stays in, with a cup over it. An eye out of its socket gets a moist sterile dressing; never push it back. For a hyphema, which is blood in the front chamber, or a ruptured globe, the book raises the head of the stretcher thirty to forty degrees and keeps the collar loose, to lower the eye pressure. And keep talking: your patient can't see you.
slides.sayZh: 受伤眼球的原则：绝不按压。压力会把玻璃体，也就是眼球后部的胶冻状物质挤出来，而且流失了不会再生。用硬质眼罩，两只眼都盖住，因为双眼是一起转动的。刺入物留在原位，上面扣一个杯子。眼球脱出眼眶时用湿的无菌敷料盖住，绝不要推回去。前房积血，也就是眼前房里出血，或眼球破裂时，书上主张把担架床头抬高三十到四十度、颈托别太紧，以降低眼压。还要不停地跟病人说话：他看不见你。

slides.title: Chemical and light burns of the eye
slides.body:
Alkali or strong acidbook: irrigate 20 minsoaks deep; keep going en route
Other chemicalsbook: at least 5 minwater or sterile saline only
UV (welding, snow)pain starts 3–5 h latermoist pad + shield, low light

BCEHS J01: flush at least 15 min (H04: saline). Never neutralize with vinegar or baking soda: the reaction makes heat. Flush from the nose side outward. Book: remove contact lenses only for a chemical burn. BCEHS H04/J01: remove them if not stuck to the cornea.
slides.say: For a chemical burn, start irrigating immediately with clean water or sterile saline. Never neutralize it with vinegar or baking soda; the reaction makes heat and worsens the burn. The book says irrigate at least five minutes, and a full twenty minutes for an alkali or a strong acid, which soak deep into the tissue. BCEHS, in J zero one, says at least fifteen minutes. Keep going en route, flushing from the nose side outward to protect the other eye. The book leaves contact lenses in, except in a chemical burn, because they trap the chemical. BCEHS goes further: gently remove contact lenses whenever they're not stuck to the cornea. Ultraviolet burns, from welding or bright snow, often don't hurt until three to five hours later. Cover them with a moist pad and a shield.
slides.sayZh: 化学烧伤要立刻用清水或无菌生理盐水冲洗。绝不要用醋或小苏打中和，中和反应会产热、加重烧伤。书上说至少冲五分钟；碱或强酸要整整冲二十分钟，它们会渗到组织深处。BCEHS 的 J01 要求至少冲十五分钟。路上继续冲，从鼻侧往外侧冲，保护另一只眼。书里说隐形眼镜一般不取，化学烧伤除外，因为镜片会困住化学品。BCEHS 更进一步：只要镜片没有粘在角膜上，就轻轻取出。紫外线烧伤，比如电焊或雪地强光，常在三到五小时后才痛。用湿垫和眼罩盖住。

slides.title: Ears and teeth
slides.body:
• Ear bleeding: soft pad behind the ear, then a roller bandage
  • Blood or CSF from the ear canal: loose dressing, don't block it
  • Torn-off ear = amputated part (BC: cool, never directly on ice)
  • Teeth: fragments are an airway risk; remove them
  • Knocked-out tooth: hold the crown, rinse gently, keep it moist
  • Book: replant within ~1 h. BCEHS H14: ASAP (PCP, age 16+); ~0% at 1 h
slides.say: For a bleeding ear, put a soft pad between the ear and the scalp, then a roller bandage around the head. Blood or clear fluid from the ear canal gets a loose dressing; don't block it. A torn-off ear is an amputated part, and BC tells you how: rinse with cool sterile water, wrap in saline-moistened sterile gauze, bag it, and keep it cool, but never directly on ice. In the mouth, broken teeth are an airway problem first. The book says a knocked-out tooth can be replanted up to about an hour later. BCEHS is more urgent: survival is best within minutes and close to zero after an hour, and a PCP may put it back, except under age sixteen. Hold the crown, not the root, rinse gently without scrubbing, and keep it moist, for example in cold milk.
slides.sayZh: 耳朵出血时，在耳朵和头皮之间垫软垫，再用卷轴绷带绕头包扎。耳道流出血或清亮液体时，用松的敷料，不要堵。被撕下的耳朵按断肢处理，BC 规定了做法：用凉的无菌水冲洗、用盐水浸湿的无菌纱布包好、装袋、保持低温，但绝不能直接放冰上。口腔里，断牙首先是气道问题。书里说，整颗脱落的牙大约一小时内仍可能再植。BCEHS 更紧迫：几分钟内放回存活率最高，超过一小时接近零；PCP 可以把牙放回牙槽，但十六岁以下不做。只拿牙冠、不碰牙根，轻轻冲洗不要刷，保持湿润，比如泡在冷牛奶里。

slides.title: The neck: critical until proven otherwise
slides.body:
Zone Ibase of the neckcan reach the chest; highest death rate
Zone IImiddlemost common, most obvious
Zone IIItop, near the skull basehard for surgeons to reach
  • Two killers: airway loss and massive bleeding
  • Stridor, hoarseness, air under the skin → larynx or trachea
  • An open neck vein can suck in air → air embolism
slides.say: The front of the neck packs the airway, the big vessels to the brain, the esophagus, and the spinal cord into a small space. Any injury there, blunt or penetrating, is critical until proven otherwise. The neck has three zones. Zone one, at the base, can extend into the chest and has the highest death rate. Zone two, the middle, is the most common and the most obvious. Zone three, near the skull base, is hard for surgeons to reach. Patients die here from losing the airway or from massive bleeding. And an open neck vein can suck in air, causing a potentially fatal air embolism.
slides.sayZh: 颈前部在很小的空间里塞进了气道、供脑的大血管、食管和脊髓。这里的任何损伤，钝伤也好穿透伤也好，在排除之前都按危重处理。颈部分三个区：一区在颈根部，可延伸进胸腔，死亡率最高；二区在中段，最常见也最明显；三区靠近颅底，外科很难处理。病人死在这里，要么是气道丢失，要么是大出血。颈部开放的静脉还可能吸入空气，造成可能致命的空气栓塞。

slides.title: Open neck wound: step by step
slides.body:
1. Seal it now: occlusive dressing (ECG electrode for a small hole)
  2. Bulky dressing + firm manual pressure
  3. Never wrap a bandage all the way round the neck
  4. Last resort: loosely round the neck, firmly under the opposite armpit
  5. Impaled object stays, unless it blocks the airway

BC: do not pack wounds on the neck, chest or abdomen. A slowing pulse may mean too much pressure on the carotid.
slides.say: For an open neck wound, seal it immediately with an occlusive dressing, so air can't be sucked into a vein. An ECG electrode works fast on a small hole. Add a bulky dressing and hold firm pressure by hand. Never wrap a bandage all the way around the neck: you could squeeze both carotid arteries or block breathing. The book's last resort is to wrap loosely around the neck and firmly under the opposite armpit. Leave impaled objects in unless they block the airway. And remember the BC rule: don't pack wounds on the neck, chest, or abdomen.
slides.sayZh: 开放性颈部伤口要立刻用封闭敷料封住，防止空气被吸进静脉；小伤口用心电电极片最快。再盖厚敷料，用手用力压住。绝不要用绷带绕颈一整圈：可能同时压住两侧颈动脉或影响呼吸。书上的最后手段是绷带松松绕过颈部、再紧紧穿过对侧腋下。刺入物留在原位，除非堵住气道。还要记住 BC 的规定：颈部、胸部、腹部的伤口不要填塞。

slides.q: A man was stabbed in the side of the neck. The wound is sealed with an occlusive dressing and you are holding pressure. HR 126, BP 84/50. Transport time is 15 minutes. As a PCP, what is your best plan?
options: Pack the wound, then start an IV on scene
Keep pressure, transport, IV en route: 20 mL/kg, reassess every 500 mL
Give 2 L of fluid on scene before moving him
Wrap a pressure bandage round the neck to free your hands
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. A man was stabbed in the side of the neck. The wound is sealed and you're holding pressure. His heart rate is one hundred twenty-six, his blood pressure eighty-four over fifty, and transport is fifteen minutes. What's your best plan? A, pack the wound, then start an IV on scene. B, keep pressure, transport, and start an IV en route, twenty millilitres per kilogram, reassessing every five hundred. C, give two litres on scene before moving him. D, wrap a pressure bandage around the neck to free your hands. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一名男子颈部侧面被刺伤，伤口已封住，你正在按压。心率一百二十六，血压八十四比五十，转运十五分钟。最好的方案是什么？A 填塞伤口，然后在现场开静脉；B 保持按压、出发，路上开静脉，每公斤二十毫升，每五百毫升复评；C 搬动前先在现场输两升；D 用绷带绕颈加压包扎，好空出手来。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Under the BC hypovolemia protocol, the PCP gets vascular access en route, or on scene only if there's a delay, and gives twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred. A is wrong because BC says not to pack neck wounds, and an IV shouldn't hold you on scene. C delays transport and skips the reassessment. D could compress both carotid arteries.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。按 BC 低血容量流程，PCP 在转运途中建立静脉通路，只有在有延误时才在现场开，补液每公斤二十毫升、最多两升，每五百毫升复评一次。A 错在 BC 规定颈部伤口不能填塞，而且开静脉不应把你留在现场；C 拖延转运，也跳过了复评；D 可能同时压住两侧颈动脉。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: face, eye and neck injuries
slides.body:
No single BC protocol: Wound Care, Spinal Management, Hypovolemia and Nausea–Vomiting apply.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Expose, examine, direct pressure
  • No packing of neck wounds
  • Stabilize impaled objects unless they block the airway
  • Spinal motion restriction: NEXUS / Canadian C-Spine
  • O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Preserve avulsed parts (cool, not on ice)

PCP adds

  • Functional enquiry incl. EENT (PCP only)
  • Shock: IV en route; 20 mL/kg, max 2 L
  • Reassess every 500 mL; consider TXA
  • Nausea: consider dimenhydrinate or ondansetron
slides.say: Several BC protocols apply here. On the left is every licence level: expose and examine, control bleeding with direct pressure but don't pack neck wounds, stabilize impaled objects unless they block the airway, restrict spinal motion using the NEXUS or Canadian C-Spine rules, give oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four or higher, and preserve avulsed parts. On the right is what's new for you: the functional enquiry, including the EENT system, eyes, ears, nose, and throat, which only PCPs do. If shock develops, an IV en route and the hypovolemia protocol, including TXA when indicated. And for nausea, dimenhydrinate or ondansetron.
slides.sayZh: 这里适用好几条 BC 流程。左栏是所有执照级别：暴露检查；直接压迫止血，但颈部伤口不填塞；刺入物除非堵气道否则原位固定；按 NEXUS 或加拿大颈椎规则限制脊柱活动；给氧使血氧维持在九十四以上；保存撕脱组织。右栏是你新增的：系统问诊，包括眼耳鼻喉系统，这只有 PCP 做。出现休克时，途中开静脉、按低血容量流程处理，有指征时包括 TXA。病人恶心时，可用茶苯海明或昂丹司琼。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Shock: book aims systolic 80–90 → BC 20 mL/kg, max 2 L, q500 mL
  • No packing of neck, chest or abdominal wounds
  • Avulsed part: cool sterile water rinse; never in water or on ice
  • Antiemetic (PCP): dimenhydrinate or ondansetron
  • Book's RSI drugs: not on the BC exam drug list
  • Suction an adult 10–15 s at a time
slides.say: For shock from a neck wound, the book aims for a systolic of eighty to ninety; for BC, use the hypovolemia numbers: twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred. BC says not to pack neck, chest, or abdominal wounds. An avulsed part is rinsed with cool sterile water, wrapped in saline-moistened gauze, bagged, and kept cool, never in water and never directly on ice. Where the book suggests an antiemetic, your BC options as a PCP are dimenhydrinate and ondansetron. The book's rapid sequence intubation drugs aren't on the BC exam drug list. And BC suctions an adult ten to fifteen seconds at a time.
slides.sayZh: 颈部伤口致休克时，书上的收缩压目标是八十到九十；BC 考试用低血容量流程的数字：每公斤二十毫升、最多两升、每五百毫升复评。BC 规定颈部、胸部、腹部伤口不填塞。撕脱的部位用凉的无菌水冲洗、盐水湿纱布包好、装袋、保持低温，绝不泡水，也绝不直接放冰上。书上建议用止吐药时，你作为 BC 的 PCP 可选茶苯海明和昂丹司琼。书上快速顺序插管用的药不在 BC 考纲药物范围内。BC 成人每次吸引十到十五秒。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Your exam goes deeper: EENT enquiry, pupils, eye movement, acuity
  • A dramatic face can hide the real threats: airway, spine, brain
  • Hidden bleeding: posterior nosebleed, older adults on blood thinners
  • IV en route: never hold a bleeding neck on scene for a line
  • Ondansetron: not in congenital long QT syndrome
  • Methoxyflurane: not with head injury or a lowered LOC
slides.say: Now, what's new for you as a PCP? First, your assessment goes deeper: the functional enquiry includes eyes, ears, nose, and throat, and with a face injury that system relates directly to the complaint, so skipping it costs marks. Second, don't let a dramatic face distract you from the airway, spine, and brain. Third, think of hidden bleeding, like a posterior nosebleed in an older patient on blood thinners. Fourth, the IV goes in en route; never hold a bleeding neck on scene for a line. Fifth, check contraindications: no ondansetron in congenital long QT syndrome, and no methoxyflurane, or Penthrox, with a head injury or a lowered level of consciousness.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲作为 PCP 新要注意的事。第一，评估更深入：系统问诊包括眼耳鼻喉，面部受伤时这个系统与主诉直接相关，漏问会扣分。第二，别让吓人的面部伤分散你对气道、脊柱和脑的注意。第三，想到隐匿出血，比如服抗凝药老人的鼻腔后部出血。第四，静脉通路途中开；绝不为开静脉把颈部出血的病人留在现场。第五，查禁忌：先天性长 QT 综合征不用昂丹司琼；头部外伤或意识水平下降时不用甲氧氟烷，也就是 Penthrox。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Face and neck: airway first; a warning of head and spine injury
  2. Never press on an injured eye; irrigate chemicals now; seal neck wounds
  3. PCP adds: EENT enquiry, IV and fluids en route, antiemetics

Next: head injuries, traumatic brain injury and the BC TBI protocol
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: a face or neck injury is an airway problem first, and a warning that the head and spine may be hurt. Two: never press on an injured eye, irrigate a chemical burn right away, and seal an open neck wound without packing it or wrapping the neck. Three: as a PCP, you add the functional enquiry with eyes, ears, nose, and throat, vascular access and fluids en route for shock, and antiemetics for nausea. Next lesson, we move to the brain: skull fractures, traumatic brain injury, and the BC TBI protocol. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 三句话收尾。一，面部或颈部损伤首先是气道问题，也在提醒你头和脊柱可能受伤。二，受伤的眼睛绝不按压，化学烧伤马上冲洗，开放的颈部伤口要封闭，但不填塞、不绕颈包扎。三，作为 PCP，你多做的是包括眼耳鼻喉的系统问诊、休克时途中开静脉补液，以及恶心时用止吐药。下节课讲脑：颅骨骨折、创伤性脑损伤和 BC 的 TBI 流程。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
